claude.rationale: This is a joint-venture pooling: both parties' tire businesses were contributed into jointly owned holding companies (each 75% Goodyear / 25% SRI), so intent is co-present (imprint-share) and the legal vehicle is newly created Netherlands/holding companies (swap); the customer-facing product operations transferred only in part, with Poland, Slovenia, Turkey, Morocco, South Africa, aircraft tires and Luxembourg technical/manufacturing assets expressly excluded (T4 subset). gap_45=1 because the slice states the acquired product operations crossed while "processes and people acquired had not yet been integrated," with plans for consolidating manufacturing, distribution, information systems and R&D "not completed" at closing — a documented product-vs-process misalignment. gap_56=1 because the same lines show operations were to be re-engineered ("downsizing or consolidation") without aligned staffing at closing, with "appropriate staffing levels" still under analysis and $80–120M severance planned, indicating people/organization not coherently aligned. gap_mitigated=no because the slice documents no transitional-services or operating agreement absorbing the shared substrate at closing — only future integration plans and SRI exit rights.

grok.rationale: gap_45=0 because the slice states that customer-facing tire manufacturing, sales and distribution businesses of both parties were contributed together into the jointly owned holding companies, so product and the processes that produce/deliver it crossed the ownership boundary together (with only expressly excluded geographies/lines staying out). gap_56=0 because the same formation disclosure records that the processes and people of the acquired businesses both crossed into the JVs at closing; although integration plans and staffing alignment were explicitly not yet completed, that is incomplete post-close integration rather than a structural transfer of processes without the organization.

openai.rationale: The tire manufacturing, sales, and distribution businesses crossed into the joint ventures together, while specified Goodyear operations remained excluded, so the slice documents no product-versus-process separation at closing. However, the filing states that integration of facilities, information systems, support functions, and staffing had not been completed, with consolidation, downsizing, and severance still contemplated, documenting a process-versus-organization alignment gap at formation. The slice does not document a transitional-services or operating agreement that contractually absorbed that specific gap at closing. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950152-99-009016, Form 10-Q (Q3 1999)]
